headline: Network models link AML transcriptomic states to treatment and ligand design
label: Network Models For Aml Therapeutics
summary: Network-based frameworks now couple transcriptomic and metabolic models to AML treatment response and candidate drug design.
synthesis: The common thread is the use of network structure derived from omics data to predict interventions in cancer, with acute myeloid leukemia as the dominant application. A functionalist edge-weighted digraph represents cytarabine treatment contextuality in AML and explores SAMHD1 inhibitors. A transcriptome-conditioned pipeline instead uses WGCNA to prioritize biomarkers, AlphaFold3 to model their structures, and metaheuristic fragment assembly to generate AML ligands, which are docking-tested. The genetic minimal intervention set framework is new in scope: it extends the genetic minimal cut set concept from knockouts to knock-ins in integrated metabolic-regulatory networks. Not every item is AML-specific, so the shared element is network-level prediction of intervention strategies rather than a single shared modeling approach.
